findings_to_judge.finding: In a Reg FD 8-K furnished 2026-07-08, GitLab restated the Duo Agent Platform paid Consumption Run Rate it had touted five weeks earlier as 'nearly $20 million' down to approximately $15 million, because the calculation 'now excludes certain one-time credit incentives granted to paying customers' - i.e. roughly a quarter of the headline AI number the street heard in June was credits given away to existing paying seats, not incremental purchase.

GitLab's FY27 guidance explicitly embeds no material Duo Agent Platform revenue contribution, yet the company went out of its way one month into Q2 to confirm paid CRR had gone from ~$15M at 30 April to above $20M at 30 June on the same restated basis - a ~33% step-up in two months on a line that is upside-only versus the guide.

GitLab 19.3, released 2026-08-20, made hard GitLab Credits usage caps generally available - subscription-level and per-user spend ceilings after which 'features that consume GitLab Credits, like GitLab Duo Agent Platform, are suspended until the next billing period' - and the same release cycle added a GitLab Dedicated AI Gateway letting enterprises connect their own inference models; both are direct concessions to customers who in GitLab's own public forum call the credit economics 'fundamentally broken' (one reported ~$10 of credits consumed by a single agentic task).

The scope of the credits wallet - and therefore of the CRR metric the market is treating as an AI-adoption gauge - is being broadened beyond AI: GitLab Secrets Manager is now 'an add-on billed through GitLab Credits' (19.3, 2026-08-20) and GitLab's own docs repository carries a commit dated 2026-08-26 titled 'Broaden GitLab Credits scope beyond Duo Agent Platform', on top of the CRR definition already having been changed once in July to add Flex and drop one-time incentives.
